Title: Real-world evidence framework to support EU regulatory decision-making - Formiventos
# Real-world evidence framework to support EU regulatory decision-making. We’re proud to share the latest progress in integrating Real-World Evidence (RWE) into regulatory decision-making; 3rd report on the experience gained with regulator-led studies from February 2024 to February 2025, aligned with the EMRN Strategy to 2028 and in collaboration with European Medicines Agency. ⏱️ Faster insights: DARWIN EU® studies had a median duration of  4 months, enabling timely regulatory input. 🔍 Quality & transparency: Enhanced data quality checks, standardized definitions, and the use of pre-approved protocols have streamlined analysis. The launch of the HMA-EMA RWD catalogues further supports transparency and collaboration. 📈 This report confirms that RWE is now a fully enabled and increasingly valuable tool across the full spectrum of regulatory use cases. 🔗 Read the full report to explore how RWE is shaping the future of medicines regulation in Europe:. ## **News & Trends**. #### Recentes. * PLANOS DE CONTINGÊNCIA em Farmacovigilncia: “Excelente formação, muito prática”. * Formação CTD MODULO 3 : ” Formação útil, clara e objetiva. Bons exemplos práticos para consolidar os conceitos abordados “. * 📢 EU Releases Updated Borderline & Classification Manual (MDR/IVDR). * Novo regulamento para notificação de efeitos indesejáveis de produtos cosméticos. * EUDAMED 2026 WORKSHOP : “Excelente formação, muito útil e prática “. * New report on the state of AI readiness in healthcare across the European Union. * Validation checklist for initial MAA under Regulation (EU) 2019/6 – biologicals other than immunologicals. * MDCG Guidance Update : Classification of Medical Devices – Revision 1.

results.title: MDR Submission for SaMD: EU and US Regulatory Overview – CENIT Consulting
results.content:
Title: MDR Submission for SaMD: EU and US Regulatory Overview – CENIT Consulting
Get your Software as a Medical Device through **EU MDR** initial submission with confidence—supported by concise context from the **US QMSR** (ISO 13485–aligned). This practical guide shows what to prepare, how to structure technical documentation (Annex II/III), and what Notified Bodies expect, so you can move efficiently toward CE marking. Rule 11 (Annex VIII) Annex II/III Tech Doc ISO 13485 QMS GSPR Matrix Notified Body Review QMSR Context (US). * Build your **Annex II/III** technical documentation with a clear, searchable index. * Map GSPRs (Annex I) to evidence with a **GSPR Matrix**. * **QMS is foundational:** MDR Article 10(9) expects a comprehensive QMS; ISO 13485 alignment also supports US *QMSR*. * **Technical File is the core:** Annex II/III requires device description, design/production, GSPR mapping, risk, V&V, clinical evaluation, and PMS plans. * **NB assessment is rigorous:** Expect QMS audit and deep review of software validation, cybersecurity, usability, and clinical evidence. Classification uses Annex VIII—**Rule 11** for software—placing most clinical decision-support software at least in Class IIa. Manufacturers must implement a QMS covering design control, risk management, clinical evaluation, PMS, and vigilance as outlined in **Article 10(9)**. The submission centers on **technical documentation** per **Annex II/III** and third-party assessment by a Notified Body for Class IIa and above. In the US, FDA requires a premarket submission (e.g., 510(k)/De Novo/PMA) and a compliant QMS; the **QMSR** aligns closely with ISO 13485, so MDR-ready systems typically map well to US expectations. 3. **Build Technical Documentation (Annex II/III)**2–4+ months. * GSPR matrix; Risk Management File; software V&V (unit/integration/system), usability & cybersecurity evidence. * Clinical Evaluation (Article 61, Annex XIV) and PMS/PMCF plans. * Focus areas: software validation completeness, cybersecurity controls, clinical evidence sufficiency, traceability. ## Evidence Pack (Annex II/III Technical Documentation). | GSPR Matrix (Annex I) | Requirement-to-evidence mapping for all applicable safety/performance clauses. | PMS / PMCF Plans (Annex III / Annex XIV Part B) | Lifecycle monitoring and evidence generation approach post-market. MDR requires a comprehensive QMS (Article 10(9)); ISO 13485 is the de-facto route and aligns with US QMSR. Successful MDR submission for SaMD hinges on accurate classification, a robust ISO 13485 QMS, and a clean, cross-referenced Annex II/III Technical File.

results.title: De Novo pre IDE Meeting - Medical Device Academy
results.content: # De Novo pre IDE Meeting. The article describes the most critical part of the preparation for a De Novo Classification Request, the De Novo pre IDE meeting.De Novo Pre-IDE Meeting Timeline and Process Flow Diagram. First, 510k clearance is based upon a substantial equivalence comparison of a device and a predicate device that is already marketed in the USA, while a De Novo classification is based upon a benefit-risk analysis of a device’s clinical benefits compared with the risk of harm to users and patients. Therefore, it makes sense that the two most common challenges for innovative medical device companies are: 1) learning how to write a benefit-risk analysis, and 2) clinical study design. ## **Benefit-risk analysis questions to ask during a De Novo pre IDE meeting**. You should review each of the alternative treatments for clinical studies that may help you in the design of your clinical study.

results.title: EU MDR: Definition, Timelines, Requirements, and Compliance
results.content: Electronic Quality Management Systems (eQMS) helps ensure EU MDR compliance in medical device economic operators. SimplerQMS offers comprehensive QMS modules covering document control, training, CAPA, audits, risk, and change management enabling medical device companies to maintain audit-ready aligned with EU MDR and ISO 13485 requirements. Compared to the Medical Device Directive (MDD), the EU MDR introduces stricter requirements for risk management, technical documentation, clinical evaluation, post-market surveillance (PMS), and transparency. * **More Detailed Technical Documentation:** EU MDR mandates expanded technical documentation, including details on risk management, device design, safety and performance, clinical evidence, labeling requirements, and manufacturing controls. EU MDR compliance means meeting all requirements under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 to ensure medical device safety, clinical performance, traceability, and post-market oversight. Moreover, EU MDR requires a formal conformity assessment process conducted by a Notified Body for most medical devices, which is a prerequisite for obtaining CE marking and legal market placement within the EU.

results.title: MDR (EU) 2017/745 | Important reminder to all manufacturers of medical devices
results.content: # MDR (EU) 2017/745 | Important reminder to all manufacturers of medical devices. ##### **We are reaching key milestones on the road to EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR)** **implementation** **for legacy devices!**. Regulation (EU) 2023/607 of 15 March 2023 amended Regulation (EU) 2017/745 for the transitional provisions for certain medical devices to give Notified Bodies (NB) the time to carry out their conformity assessments and **avoid shortages of devices**. At Archer Research, as specialized Medical Device CRO, we understand the EU MDR clinical requirements and deadlines, and we are there to advise and guide our clients. * The **technical documentation** required for the conformity assessment procedure for certain medical devices must include, among other documentation, **sufficient clinical evidence** resulting from post-market surveillance and clinical follow-up (PMCF) data. + With extended expertise in the medical device industry, Archer Research can help manufacturers evaluate their **gaps in clinical evidence** and provide support to design and conduct studies that meet their needs in a timely-manner, while ensuring cost-efficiency.
